svg.title: Contain threats through network segmentation
svg.desc: Target architecture for the in-progress OPNsense home network project. OPNsense connects to the internet, enforces default-deny inter-zone rules with explicit exceptions, filters outbound traffic and logs denied connections. Suricata starts in IDS alert mode, with blocking planned after tuning. WireGuard terminates remote tunnels on the firewall and applies access rules per peer. An 802.1Q trunk connects the firewall to a managed switch. Five distinct VLAN zones are CORE-MGMT, TRUST-WORK, IOT-CAGE, GUEST-OPEN and the planned LAB-REDZONE. A multi-SSID access point maps wireless networks to VLANs. The drawing shows connections and zone purposes, not a full permission matrix or proof that the rollout is complete. Specific WORK-to-IoT and WORK-to-LAB rules remain subject to the unresolved differences between the source prose and matrix. Source: network-segmentation/README.md.
svg.text: Route traffic between zones through explicit firewall rules.
Between zones: deny unless explicitly allowed
Filter outbound traffic · log denied connections
Limit how far a compromised device can reach beyond its zone.
Lines show network connections; access between zones depends on firewall rules.
Rollout incomplete · LAB and IPS blocking planned
